reflexion_entries_to_archive.note: HANDOFF_S133 and THREE save.ts docblocks all said the creature-lifetime fix belonged in serializeCreature emit condition. All four were wrong: netSnapshot post-trims, so an emit-only change leaves the wire byte-identical AND leaves the whole suite green, because the existing characterization asserts through netSnapshot. The carried instruction was not just incomplete, it was self-concealing. Re-derive a logged fix LOCATION from source, never inherit it.

Everyone framed this as a host-migration bug. The Council synthesis measured a third consumer nobody named: main.ts -> workerSim restore() + isHost=true runs the DISK serializer, so a Voltkin lifetime died on the ORIGINAL host under ?worker=1, no peer involved. Live on today build, and V6-1.1 flips ?worker=1 default-on. Ask which consumers share a serializer before scoping any serialization fix.

First run: all three mutations reported ANCHOR MATCHED 0 TIMES because save.ts is pure CRLF and my anchors used bare LF — only caught because I had built an anchor-count guard that refuses to report an unapplied mutation. Second run: M2/M3 passed 8/8 against deliberately broken code because no fixture creature had a targetCreatureId, so every creature took trimMirrorCreature EARLY RETURN and the mutation sat in dead code. That is the S133 M9 lesson repeating on me one session later. A mutation that passes is not evidence the guard works until you prove the mutated line EXECUTED.

The creature deletion was MASKING the sourceSpawnerId strip: while creatures are deleted you cannot observe that per-spawner caps are disabled or that a rehydrated chewer blocks its owner Voltkin summon. Shipping the lifetime fix alone would have traded one loud bug for two silent, ungatable ones. When a fix makes previously-dead state reachable, enumerate what starts running.

The load-bearing evidence was not that all three mutations went red — it was that under M2 TEST A STAYED GREEN while B/B2/C went red. That asymmetry is what demonstrates the two edits repair different consumers. A matrix where every mutation reds everything proves far less than one that reds a specific, predicted subset.

Six turns of dense project shorthand (PRIME-AUDIT, A.0, carriers, tiers) and the owner said outright he had no idea what I was doing. The work was sound and the communication was useless, which makes the work useless. He also pointed out the game looks identical to two weeks ago — true, and I should have led with that rather than with a PDR. Lead with plain English and with what changed for the player.

Justified here — the A.0 and the Council each independently caught a BLOCKER that would have shipped a green no-op — but the ratio should be named, not hidden: deliberation cost ~100x the diff.

The Council synthesis found a third consumer (worker INIT) that none of its three position-holders found, by MEASURING rather than reasoning. That reframed the bug from theoretical-on-migration to live-on-today-build.
The mutation harness anchor-count guard paid for itself immediately — it refused to report three CRLF no-op mutations as passes.

owner_rulings_s134.B4_directives: AMENDED — an ordered RTS-style BUILD QUEUE of individual primitives, NOT a filter. Click a shape N times => xN queued; ordered and consumed (leftmost next, each delivery pops one); ONE queue per player; empty queue => gatherers collect nearest (priority override, not on/off); bank full => a loaded gatherer walks home and WAITS at the castle holding its item, depositing the moment a slot frees; all controls live in a FOOTER BAR at the bottom of the screen.
